title: Regeneration is ordinary growth, with the same curve as growth from zero

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Regeneration is ordinary growth, with the same curve as growth from zero

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Regeneration is a particular case of growth obeying the same laws; the regeneration curve (short latent period, rapid rise to a maximum velocity, then slow decline) only appears different because ordinary growth curves start at birth, and a complete growth curve from zero has the same essential features.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. III: The Rate of Growth

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: A complete curve of growth, starting from zero, has the same essential characteristics as the regeneration curve.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter III, “The Rate of Growth”; topic “Regeneration”. Scope: regenerating tissues and whole-organism growth

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch03-31: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Curve features can be quantified, but the asserted equivalence is qualitative and spans unlike processes. Existing data permit comparisons in selected systems, not a decisive general test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Normalize complete regeneration and whole-organism growth trajectories and compare their latent, accelerating, peak-velocity, and decelerating phases using shared versus separate curve families. Support requires a common curve structure across matched tissues or taxa; systematic phase or shape differences refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Same essential characteristics' permits multiple interpretations.

Normalization can conceal biologically important differences.

Matched regeneration and zero-origin ontogeny data are rare.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Ordinary growth curves are easy to obtain, and the qualitative shape Thompson names can be scored. Regeneration series are not in the same archives, and the early limb he treats as decisive is the part most often missing. Because the likeness is defined loosely, many discordant curves would still be called the same essential shape.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Align regeneration curves and whole-organism growth curves on a common time origin at the start of growth, and compare the sequence latent period, rise to a velocity maximum, then slow decline. Matching sequence and comparable scaled shape would support the claim; a regeneration curve that stays monotonic, or a full growth curve that lacks the rising limb, would refute a shared shape.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Regeneration lengths are scattered across papers and start after a latent period that is poorly sampled.

'Essential features' does not specify a numerical tolerance.

Many unrelated processes share a rise-and-fall velocity curve.
